decisions.reason: Requiring comprehension by unfamiliar viewers changes content completeness, not how source moments are selected. The B-roll instruction is independently represented and does not replace the long-form source material.
Standalone comprehension for unfamiliar viewers does not modify the existing effective-hook requirement.
The comprehension requirement does not add, remove, or change any target publication channel.
The source message independently establishes the music rule, but the source Requirement's comprehension change does not modify that rule and a same-message music Event already exists.
The initial three-clip trial is a separate historical assignment; the new comprehension standard does not alter its task-local state.

The five-clip live batch already has a same-message introduction. The unfamiliar-viewer standard applies through the separate content Requirement and does not change the batch's count or deliverable attributes.
Viewer comprehension does not modify the clean-editing or effects policies; the source's clean-editing clause is an independent reaffirmation.
The unfamiliar-viewer comprehension change does not alter the existing white-text, font, or caption-effects rules.
The source introduces a new first-live batch and a general comprehension standard, not a change to the earlier task-local requalification assignment.
The requirement that the client review clips before publication is consistent with the existing approval gate and introduces no new approval authority, eligibility rule, or rejection behavior.
Natural B-roll integration is independently established by the same message, but it is not changed by the source Requirement's unfamiliar-viewer comprehension update.
The unfamiliar-viewer comprehension requirement does not change the existing 45-to-60-second duration range.
